marks.gloss_en: והיכי משכחת לה? -- how could a carcass be too hard [for dogs] to eat?
בבשר פילי -- elephant flesh
אי נמי בגורייאתא זוטרי -- alternatively, young puppies
אמר לך רב יהודה: לא, נבלה דומיא דדלועין -- the carcass is like the pumpkins, hard (= p_yehuda_nevela_ashuna)
no: the carcass is like the pumpkins -- as the pumpkins are hard, so the carcass is hard
תא שמע, דתני רב חנן מנהרדעא: מפרכין תבן ואספסתא ומערבין -- אלמא טרחינן באוכלא
תבן בתיבנא סריא, אספסתא בעילי זוטרי -- the straw is rotten straw, the alfalfa [is crumbled] for young donkeys
one may crumble straw and alfalfa and mix [them]
וכדאמר רב ירמיה מדיפתי: an Arab fed his camel a kor and loaded it with a kor -- so such feeding occurs
מי איכא כי האי גוונא? -- is there such a thing [as feeding a camel so much]?
אין -- yes (= p_ika_kehai_gavna)
what is 'one may not stuff'? Rav Yehuda: one may not make a trough for it inside its stomach
the mishna: one may not stuff (אובסין) a camel
דתניא בהדיא: רבי יוסי בר יהודה אומר נותנין מים למורסן -- explicitly of bran

דילמא עד כאן לא קאמר רבי יוסי בר יהודה התם אלא קמח דבר גיבול הוא, אבל מורסן דלאו בר גיבול הוא אפילו רבי יוסי בר יהודה מודה -- perhaps he spoke only of flour, which is kneadable; of bran even he concedes
לא סלקא דעתא, דתניא בהדיא: אין נותנין מים למורסן, דברי רבי; רבי יוסי בר יהודה אומר: נותנין מים למורסן
Rabbi: one may not put water to bran
Rabba (Abaye's Master): our mishna [one may put water to bran but not knead] is R' Yosei bar Yehuda's
דתניא: R' Yosei bar Yehuda -- not liable until he kneads (against Rabbi, the latter is liable)
the baraita: one may not knead kali
כדתניא: food before a dog, not before a pig -- this one's sustenance is on you, that one's is not
אמר לך רב יהודה: mehalketin is by hand and malkitin throwing; the doves are forbidden even throwing because their sustenance is not on you, unlike chickens (= p_mezonotan_alecha)
these [chickens], their sustenance is on you; those [doves], their sustenance is not on you -- so even throwing food before the doves is not permitted
מתניתין נמי דייקא: no water before bees and dovecote doves, but before geese, chickens and hardisian doves -- is it not because of whose sustenance is on you?
the mishna: one does not put water before bees or dovecote doves, but one does before geese, chickens and hardisian doves
ולטעמיך, why specifically water? even wheat and barley should be forbidden! rather, water is different, for it is found in the lake
כדתנן: a dog's food stays in its innards three full days
R' Yona: the Holy One knows the dog's food is scarce, therefore its food stays in its innards three days
שמע מינה -- from R' Yona's derasha
Rav Hamnuna: it is proper conduct to throw a piece of meat to a dog
תניא כוותיה דרב יהודה: hamra'a -- laid down, mouth forced open, vetch and water at once; halata -- standing, each separately
hamra'a: one lays it down, forces its mouth open and feeds it vetch and water at once; halata: one feeds it standing and waters it standing, vetch separately and water separately

מתיב רב יוסף: if mehalketin is feeding by hand and malkitin throwing before them, then even throwing before dovecote doves would be forbidden?! rather mehalketin is into a place it cannot bring back and malkitin a place it can -- so (mehalketin being permitted) hamra'a must be with a vessel, ותיובתא דרב יהודה (155b.6-7)
one may mehalketin chickens, and needless to say malkitin; one may not malkitin dovecote doves or attic doves, and needless to say not mehalketin
the mishna: one may not do hamra'a [to an animal on Shabbat]
